title: Habits & activities
intro: Track any behavior: choose a preset or define your own. Keep a consistent definition of one event, such as one cigarette or one reading session. These are recording categories, not recommendations or proven longevity interventions.
semantics: Blank means unknown; 0 means the activity did not occur. Removing a row also removes it from your routine for new days. Keep the row and switch off its routine checkbox to stop repeating it without losing today’s observation.
noMatches: No matches. Define your own activity below.
customLibrary: Create your own activity & manage your library
customHelp: Custom names are saved to your private library and stay in their original language. Daily observations are saved with the check-in.
archiveHelp: Archiving hides a category from new selections. It keeps all recorded observations and analysis inputs.
remove: Remove {{name}} from this day and routine
timeHelp: Use the journal day and its time zone. You may record only the times you remember; the daily count can be larger. Repeated times are allowed.
analysisHelp: Recorded habits appear in Choose inputs: counts, minutes and complete event-time cycles. Their absence on a day stays unknown.
privacy: Your private activity library and daily counts, local event times, durations and optional notes are stored in the database. Archiving a category keeps its history; deleting your account removes the library and observations from the active database. Check-in review runs in your browser using earlier numerical observations, not narrative notes.
guide: Counts and total minutes can be used as inputs in Relationships and Multivariable predictions. Complete event times are encoded as mean sine and cosine around a 24-hour clock; select both. An evening behavior belongs to its calendar date, while sleep belongs to the waking date: use a one-day lag to explore the following night. These categories do not establish health benefits or harms; synthetic demo relationships are constructed examples.
openCheckIn: Record an activity in Daily check-in
reviewGuide: Review compares an entry with earlier observations; unusual is not incorrect. At least 30 comparable measurements are needed, and any notice can be confirmed without changing your values. A lack of notices is not a validation of the entry.
